2,110 likes, 122 comments - fit_foodie_lulu on July 26, 2026: "DECONSTRUCTED WONTON SOUP 🍜 Homemade wontons without the effort! Juicy flavour-packed chicken meatballs, bold broth, loads of veggies, and garnish with a kick of chili oil. One pot wonder. So much umami.

Macros (serves 4 people)
• 394 kcal
• 41g P
• 35g C
• 9g F

Chicken meatballs
• 500g chicken breast mince
• 2 tsp sesame oil
• 2 garlic cloves, minced
• 1 tbsp ginger paste
• 1.5 tbsp soy sauce
• ¼ tsp white pepper
• 2 spring onions, finely chopped

Soup
• 1 tbsp sesame oil
• 4 garlic cloves minced
• 1 tbsp ginger paste
• 4 spring onions thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)
• 6 cups reduced-salt chicken broth
• 2 tbsp soy sauce
• 2 tsp coconut sugar
• 2 tbsp Chinese cooking wine
• 1 large carrot, julienned
• 250g shiitake mushrooms (or white) sliced
• 2 bunches baby Bok choy, chopped
• 20 wonton wrappers, cut in half
Garnish: Chili oil and extra green onions

 
Method
1. Mix all chicken wonton ingredients together. You can form into small meatballs (about 1 heaped tsp each) or simply use 2 spoons to form balls and drop them into the soup later like I did in the video. The mixture will be wet -don’t worry!

2. In a large pot over medium heat, add sesame oil. Sauté garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites for 2 minutes until nice and fragrant.

3. Add chicken broth, soy sauce, coconut sugar, and Chinese cooking wine. Cover and simmer gently for 10 mins to let the flavours infuse.

4. Drop in the meatballs, carrot and mushrooms. Boil for 3 mins.

5. Add wonton wrappers a few at a time, then stir, (to prevent them sticking together), stir then add Bok choy. Simmer for 2 more minutes.

6. Ladle into bowls. Drizzle with chili oil and top with the green spring onions. Serve hot!".

audio.transcript: You love homemade wontons but can't be bothered folding them. This recipe is for you. This deconstructed wonton soup has all the flavor, is ready in under 30 minutes, and packs over 40 grams of protein for under 400 calories per serve. Honestly, it's one of the best soups I've ever made. You definitely have to try it.
